bounds.domain: Eight boot phases and two deferred task identities. A separate retirement projection has one outgoing and one active replacement runtime, a shared or distinct adapter, one initially active write or no write, and two original service-stop callbacks.
bounds.scope: Finite boot/teardown safety and conditional retirement progress. Fast completion and lookup clearing do not release callback ownership. The retirement receipt is the host helper's resolution/rejection; the CLI reports cleanup failure after publishing its replacement. Real HTTP, file-backed SQLite scheduler/retention, shared PGlite and distinct PGlite conformance.

assumptions: Weak fairness of advance: accepted storage work eventually succeeds or fails, each original stop callback settles, the fast-stop continuation and strict-retirement continuation run, and host cleanup settles.

Escalation cleanup and adapter closure are abstracted as a settling host cleanup step. Callback failure produces a failed receipt after drain. This is not a wall-clock bound or a proof of process-signal exit.
No fairness is assumed. A callback whose accepted storage work never settles can retain the outgoing adapter indefinitely; the fast cap does not prove retirement.
